title: Bolstering the Security of Digital Banking
what_it_is: Bolstering the Security of Digital Banking

sections.label: OCBC phishing scam losses
sections.summary: 790 OCBC customers lost $13.7 million to scammers, mostly from 23 to 30 December, in the most serious spoofed-SMS phishing scam seen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Seven hundred ninety OCBC customers lost a total of $13.7 million to the scammers, mostly over the year-end festive period from 23 December to 30 December.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is by far the most serious phishing scam we have seen involving spoofed SMSes impersonating banks.

sections.label: OCBC full reimbursement
sections.summary: As a one-off goodwill gesture, the bank will reimburse all affected customers in full; over 90% have been paid.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As a one-off goodwill gesture, the bank has undertaken to reimburse in full all customers affected by this phishing scam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To date, more than 90% of them have received reimbursements and the remaining reimbursements should be disbursed soon.

sections.label: Bank remedial action timelines
sections.summary: Banks committed to timelines for remedial actions, most by June 2022 and IT-heavy changes by December 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The banks had committed to timelines to take these remedial actions, with most measures to be fully implemented by June 2022, while those requiring extensive changes in IT systems to be completed by December 2022, at the latest.

sections.label: MAS ABS anti-scam measures
sections.summary: MAS and ABS announced measures on 19 January 2022 for immediate implementation, including removing clickable links and 24/7 call centre teams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As an urgent first step in this process, MAS and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) announced a set of additional measures on 19 January 2022 for immediate implementation by retail banks in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The measures include removing clickable links in all bank emails and SMSes sent to retail customers; delaying by at least 12 hours before a new soft token can be activated on a mobile device; lowering to $100 or below the default threshold for sending transaction notifications to customers; sending a notification alert to the customer’s existing mobile number or email registered with the bank whenever there is a request for change; sending scam alerts directly to customers through email or SMS; and setting up dedicated call centre teams on a 24/7 basis to assist customers facing a potential scam and to freeze compromised accounts immediately to prevent further illicit withdrawals.

sections.label: AI detection of suspicious transactions
sections.summary: MAS will expect banks to develop more versatile algorithms using artificial intelligence and machine learning to detect suspicious transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Beyond pre-defined parameters, MAS will expect banks to develop more versatile algorithms employing artificial intelligence and machine learning to detect suspicious transactions.

sections.label: Customer confirmations for high-risk transactions
sections.summary: MAS and banks are looking to introduce additional customer confirmations for significant account changes or high-risk transactions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, MAS and the banks are looking to introduce additional customer confirmations – not just notifications – for significant changes to their accounts or high-risk transactions, such as changes in account holder details, activating a token on another device, fund transfers that are large relative to their overall balances and overseas transfers.

sections.label: Disputed transactions and credit records
sections.summary: Disputed transactions will not adversely affect consumers' credit records with licensed credit bureaus during the investigation period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Disputed transactions will not adversely affect consumers’ credit records with licensed credit bureaus during the investigation period.

sections.label: Payments Council scam loss framework
sections.summary: The Payments Council chaired by MAS has been working on a framework for equitable sharing of losses arising from scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Payments Council chaired by MAS has been working on a framework for equitable sharing of losses arising from scams.

sections.label: Framework public consultation timeline
sections.summary: MAS aims to publish the framework for public consultation within the next three months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: MAS aims to publish the framework for public consultation within the next three months.

sections.label: Ministerial Statements and clarifications
sections.summary: The Minister for Communications and Information and Minister of State for Home Affairs will make related Ministerial Statements, with clarifications allowed after the third Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister for Communications and Information and Minister of State for Home Affairs will be making related Ministerial Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarifications on all three Statements after the third Statement.
